title: Sectionwise comparison of the concrete module-sheaf Cech complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a type in its universe, $U:I\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ any family and $F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $D$ and $a:F\to D^0$ be the concrete constructions of [def-pc-cech-module-sheaf-functor]. Let $G$ forget module sheaves to presheaves of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$-modules. Put $Q(W)(V)=F(W\times V)$ with restriction of global scalars and restriction maps in both variables, and $C=\check C^\bullet(U,Q)$. There exist isomorphisms $e_p:G(D^p)\simeq C^p$ satisfying $G(d_D^p)e_{p+1}=e_p d_C^p$. Moreover, for every $y:\mathrm{Fin}(1)\to I$ and open $V$, the $y$-coordinate of $G(a)e_0$ on $V$ is the restriction $F(V)\to F((\prod_l U(y(l)))\times V)$ along the second projection. No cover assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Use the real intersection sheaf functor of [def-pc-cech-module-sheaf-functor]. Its scalar restriction on V is the composite of restriction from global functions to V and from V to W times V. ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp'App identifies it with direct restriction to W times V. The equality of ring maps follows because opens form a thin category. The maps of underlying groups are identities, hence these comparisons are natural in V and W.

The functor G preserves products: after evaluation on V it is SheafOfModules.evaluation followed by restriction of scalars, both of which preserve the relevant limits. Apply preservesLimitsOfShape_of_evaluation. For any opposite formal coproduct T, asIso(piComparison G ...) gives the product comparison. Projection equations prove its naturality in T using evalOp and functoriality of G.

Whisker that natural product comparison by the formal Cech cosimplicial object and compose with evalOp applied to the scalar comparison. Its degree components are the desired e_p. Naturality at each simplex coface proves coface compatibility. G is additive; expand both differentials as alternating sums and use map_sum, map_zsmul and coface compatibility to obtain the differential identity.

Project the degree-zero map to y. The product comparison projection equation gives G(a followed by the y projection). Pi.lift_π makes this the adjunction unit at the categorical tuple product. On V the over-site adjunction unit is F.map prod.snd.op; scalar comparison has identity underlying maps, which gives the coordinate equation. Empty I gives empty products, and coordinate assertions are vacuous.

theorem exists_cechModuleSheafComparison
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (F : X.Modules) :
    ∃ (e : ∀ p : ℕ,
      (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).obj
          ((cechModuleSheafComplex U F).X p).val ≅
        ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
          ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).X p),
      (∀ p : ℕ,
        (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            ((cechModuleSheafComplex U F).d p (p + 1)).val ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
            ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).d p (p + 1)) ∧
      (∀ (y : Fin 1 → ι) (V : X.Opens),
        ((PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            (cechModuleSheafAugmentation₀ U F).val ≫ (e 0).hom ≫
          Pi.π (fun y : Fin 1 → ι =>
            ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat).obj
                (op (∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)))) y).app (op V) =
          F.presheafModuleCat.map (prod.snd : (∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)) ⨯ V ⟶ V).op)
